claim: Fusion of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) with the plasma membrane results in the secretion of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs), or exosomes.
source: Fusion of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) with the plasma membrane results in the secretion of intraluminal vesicles (ILVs), or exosomes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about exosome biogenesis.

claim: The sorting of one exosomal cargo RNA, miR223, is facilitated by the RNA-binding protein, YBX1.
source: The sorting of one exosomal cargo RNA, miR223, is facilitated by the RNA-binding protein, YBX1 (Shurtleff et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work by Shurtleff et al., 2016.

claim: miR223 specifically binds a 'cold shock' domain (CSD) of YBX1 through a 5' proximal sequence motif UCAGU.
source: We found that miR223 specifically binds a 'cold shock' domain (CSD) of YBX1 through a 5' proximal sequence motif UCAGU that may represent a binding site or structural feature required for sorting.
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 2.

claim: Most of the cytoplasmic miR223 resides in mitochondria prior to sorting into exosomes.
source: Prior to sorting into exosomes, most of the cytoplasmic miR223 resides in mitochondria.
evidence: Supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: YBAP1, an RNA-binding protein localized to the mitochondrial matrix, appears to serve as a negative regulator of miR223 enrichment into exosomes.
source: An RNA-binding protein localized to the mitochondrial matrix, YBAP1, appears to serve as a negative regulator of miR223 enrichment into exosomes.
evidence: Supported by data showing increased exosomal miR223 in YBAP1 KO cells (Figure 5).

claim: miR223 levels decreased in the mitochondria and increased in exosomes after loss of YBAP1.
source: miR223 levels decreased in the mitochondria and increased in exosomes after loss of YBAP1.
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from YBAP1 KO cells shown in Figure 5.

claim: YBX1 shuttles between mitochondria and endosomes in live cells.
source: We observed YBX1 shuttle between mitochondria and endosomes in live cells.
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 6.

claim: YBX1 partitions into P body granules in the cytoplasm.
source: YBX1 also partitions into P body granules in the cytoplasm (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2021.

claim: Microvesicles released by budding from the plasma membrane are a heterogeneous population of EVs ranging in size from 30 nm to 1000 nm.
source: Microvesicles released by budding from the plasma membrane are a heterogeneous population of EVs ranging in size from 30 nm to 1000 nm (Cocucci et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cocucci et al., 2009.

claim: Exosomes are 30 nm to 150 nm in size and originate as vesicles invaginated into the interior of an MVB to form intraluminal vesicles.
source: Exosomes are 30 nm to 150 nm in size and originate as vesicles invaginated into the interior of an MVB to form intraluminal vesicles (ILVs; Harding et al., 1983).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harding et al., 1983.

claim: Many RNAs are selectively sorted into EVs, especially small RNAs.
source: Many RNAs are selectively sorted into EVs, especially small RNAs.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: RNA binding proteins (RNPs) may be involved in the enrichment of RNAs into EVs.
source: Several studies have indicated that RNA binding proteins (RNPs) may be involved in the enrichment of RNAs into EVs (Mukherjee et al., 2016; Santangelo et al., 2016; Teng et al., 2017; Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: EVs form two distinct populations of high and low buoyant density.
source: To address this question, we previously developed buoyant density-based methods to separate EVs from non-vesicular aggregates and found that EVs form two distinct populations of high and low buoyant density (Shurtleff et al., 2016; Temoche-Diaz et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work by Shurtleff et al., 2016 and Temoche-Diaz et al., 2020.

claim: Some miRNAs are selectively enriched in a high buoyant density vesicle fraction characterized by an enrichment in the exosomal marker protein CD63.
source: We found that some miRNAs are selectively enriched in a high buoyant density vesicle fraction characterized by an enrichment in the exosomal marker protein CD63, whereas the low buoyant density EVs are fairly non-selective in the capture of miRNAs (Temoche-Diaz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Temoche-Diaz et al., 2019.

claim: Phase separated YBX1 condensates selectively recruit miR223 in vitro and sort it into exosomes in cells.
source: We subsequently found that phase separated YBX1 condensates selectively recruit miR223 in vitro and sort it into exosomes in cells (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2021.

claim: Exosomal miR223 is decreased in YBX1 knockout cells.
source: We reexamined the enrichment and confirmed that exosomal miR223 was decreased in exosomes purified from YBX1 KO cells (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Knockout of YBX1 did not affect exosome secretion.
source: We used a Nanosight particle tracking device to quantify buoyant density purified vesicles and found that knockout of YBX1 did not affect exosome secretion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by Nanosight particle tracking data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: YBX1 directly and specifically binds to miR223 with a Kd of 4.2 nM.
source: The EMSA data showed that YBX1 directly and specifically bound to miR223, but ~140 fold less well with miR190 (Figure 1b–c). The measured Kd for YBX1:miR223 was 4.2 nM (Figure 1d).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1b-d.

claim: YBX1 binds miR190 approximately 140-fold less well than miR223.
source: The EMSA data showed that YBX1 directly and specifically bound to miR223, but ~140 fold less well with miR190 (Figure 1b–c).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: YBX1 has three major domains including an N-terminal alanine/proline-rich (A/P) domain, a central cold shock domain (CSD) and a C-terminal domain (CTD).
source: YBX1 has three major domains including an N-terminal alanine/proline-rich (A/P) domain, a central cold shock domain (CSD) and a C-terminal domain (CTD) (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is a description of the known domain structure of YBX1, illustrated in Figure 1e.

claim: The A/P domain and CTD of YBX1 have little or no affinity for miR223.
source: EMSA data showed that the A/P domain and CTD had little or no affinity for miR223, whereas the CSD domain bound miR223 but with an affinity much reduced compared to full length YBX1 (Figure 1f).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The CSD domain of YBX1 binds miR223 but with reduced affinity compared to full length YBX1.
source: EMSA data showed that the A/P domain and CTD had little or no affinity for miR223, whereas the CSD domain bound miR223 but with an affinity much reduced compared to full length YBX1 (Figure 1f).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The A/P domain of YBX1 is dispensable for miR223 binding.
source: The EMSA data showed that the A/P domain was dispensable, whereas binding of miR223 to CSD plus CTD was comparable to full-length YBX1 (Figure 1g).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Binding of miR223 to CSD plus CTD is comparable to full-length YBX1.
source: The EMSA data showed that the A/P domain was dispensable, whereas binding of miR223 to CSD plus CTD was comparable to full-length YBX1 (Figure 1g).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: YBX1-F85A mutation blocks the YBX1-specific binding of mRNA.
source: YBX1-F85A in the CSD domain was reported to block the YBX1-specific binding of mRNA (Lyons et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lyons et al., 2016.

claim: Purified YBX1-F85A protein fails to bind miR223.
source: Purified YBX1-F85A protein failed to bind miR223 (Figure 1g, Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 1g and Figure 1—figure supplement 2c.

claim: YBX1 directly and specifically binds miR223 via the CSD.
source: These data suggest that YBX1 directly and specifically binds miR223 via the CSD.
evidence: This is an inference based on the EMSA data with YBX1 domains and mutants.

claim: The CTD of YBX1 does not bind miR223 but may facilitate a higher affinity interaction of the CSD with miR223.
source: The CTD of YBX1 did not appear to bind miR223 but may somehow facilitate a higher affinity interaction of the CSD with miR223.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that CSD+CTD binds better than CSD alone.

claim: The sequence UCAGU on miR223 is critical for interaction with YBX1.
source: Using this EMSA competition assay to screen the miR223 binding motif, we found that the competitive binding of miR223mut (3-6) and miR223mut (4-7) were decreased (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). This suggested that the sequence UCAGU was critical for interaction with YBX1.
evidence: Supported by EMSA competition assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Substitution of UCAGU with AGACA in miR223 results in approximately 27-fold reduced YBX1 interaction.
source: EMSA data showed a~27-fold reduced YBX1 interaction of with miR223mut, whereas the affinity of miR190sort with YBX1 was increased ~eightfold compared to wt sequences.
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2b-c.

claim: Substitution of AUAUG with UCAGU in miR190 increases YBX1 affinity approximately eightfold.
source: EMSA data showed a~27-fold reduced YBX1 interaction of with miR223mut, whereas the affinity of miR190sort with YBX1 was increased ~eightfold compared to wt sequences.
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2b-c.

claim: The level of miR223 in exosomes is approximately fourfold dependent on the UCAGU sorting motif.
source: RT-qPCR data showed that the level of miR223 in exosomes was ~fourfold dependent on the putative exosomal sorting motif (Figure 3e)
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2e (note: text says Figure 3e but this appears to be a typo).

claim: The enrichment of miR190sort into exosomes is increased approximately fivefold compared to miR190 WT.
source: and the enrichment of miR190sort into exosomes was increased ~fivefold compared to miR190 WT (Figure 2f).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The UCAGU motif is critical for miR223 packaging into vesicles in the cell-free reaction.
source: The results suggested that the UCAGU motif is critical for miR223 packaging into vesicles in the cell-free reaction.
evidence: Supported by in vitro packaging assay data shown in Figure 2g-h.

claim: miR223 but not miR190 is significantly enriched in mitochondria.
source: Analysis of RNA extracted from isolated membranous organelles confirmed that miR223 but not miR190 was significantly enriched in mitochondria but not in ER or cytosol (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from subcellular fractionation shown in Figure 3b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, and citation to Wang et al., 2020.

claim: miR223 is enriched in mitoplasts along with mRNA for COX1, but not with nuclear U6 snRNA.
source: RNA was extracted from the purified mitoplast and RT-qPCR data indicated that miR223 was enriched along with mRNA for COX1, but not with nuclear U6 snRNA (Figure 3d).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: miR223 is enclosed within mitochondria, possibly in association with the inner membrane.
source: We conclude that miR223 is enclosed within mitochondria, possibly in association with the inner membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on mitoplast purification and fractionation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: CCCP treatment causes mitochondria to be removed by mitophagy in U-2 OS cells expressing GFP-parkin.
source: U-2 OS cells expressing GFP-parkin were treated with CCCP for 48 hr, conditions that cause mitochondria to be removed by mitophagy.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CCCP-induced mitophagy in Parkin-expressing cells.

claim: miR223, but not miR190, increases threefold in cells treated with CCCP.
source: RT-qPCR data showed that miR223, but not miR190, increased threefold in cells treated with CCCP (Figure 3j).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3j.

claim: Exosome secretion does not change after CCCP treatment.
source: Although exosome secretion, as measured with a CD63-luciferase marker, did not change after CCCP treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a), we found that CCCP treatment lowered the amount of miR223 in EVs fourfold (Figure 3j).
evidence: Supported by CD63-Nluc luminescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2a.

claim: CCCP treatment lowers the amount of miR223 in EVs fourfold.
source: Although exosome secretion, as measured with a CD63-luciferase marker, did not change after CCCP treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a), we found that CCCP treatment lowered the amount of miR223 in EVs fourfold (Figure 3j).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3j.

claim: The increase in cellular miR223 at the expense of exosomal miR223 after CCCP treatment may reflect a critical role for mitochondria in the mobilization of this RNA to exosomes.
source: The increase in cellular at the expense of exosomal miR223 may reflect a critical role for mitochondria in the mobilization of this RNA to exosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mitochondrial depletion increases cellular and decreases exosomal miR223.

claim: YBAP1 copurifies with YBX1 from 293T cells.
source: In the course of purifying a tagged version of YBX1 from 293T cells, we observed another protein that copurified and found that it corresponded to YBAP1 (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: Supported by protein purification and immunoblot data shown in Figure 4a-b.

claim: A complex of YBX1 and YBAP1 has previously been reported.
source: Such a complex of YBX1 and YBAP1 has previously been reported (Matsumoto et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Matsumoto et al., 2005.

claim: Purified YBX1 and YBAP1 bind each other when coexpressed in insect cells.
source: We confirmed that purified YBX1 and YBAP1 bind each other by coexpression and affinity purification from insect cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by copurification data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: YBAP1 is a mitochondrial matrix protein with a standard N-terminal transit peptide sequence.
source: YBAP1 is a mitochondrial matrix protein with a standard N-terminal transit peptide sequence (Muta et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Muta et al., 1997.

claim: YBAP1 is localized within mitochondria.
source: We also showed that YBAP1 is localized within mitochondria by performing a proteinase K protection assay on purified mitochondria.
evidence: Supported by proteinase K protection assay data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: YBAP1 is resistant to proteinase K digestion in intact mitochondria.
source: YBAP1 was resistant to proteinase K digestion as was the mitochondrial inner membrane marker Tim23. Both were degraded by proteinase treatment in the presence of Triton X-100 (Figure 4e), consistent with the localization of YBAP1 within mitochondria.
evidence: Supported by proteinase K protection assay data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Mitochondrial miR223 is immunoprecipitated by YBAP1 antibody but not by a control antibody.
source: RT qPCR data showed that mitochondrial miR223 was immunoprecipitated by YBAP1 antibody but not by a control antibody (Figure 4g).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from YBAP1 immunoprecipitation shown in Figure 4g.

claim: Purified YBAP1 binds miR223, but not miR190.
source: To determine whether the YBAP1 and miR223 interaction was direct, we used the EMSA assay and found that purified YBAP1 bound miR223, but not miR190.
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4h-j.

claim: The YBAP1 interaction with miR223 is not dependent on the RNA sequence motif responsible for YBX1 binding.
source: The YBAP1 interaction with miR223 was not dependent on the RNA sequence motif responsible for YBX1 binding (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a–b).
evidence: Supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a-b.

claim: YBAP1 binds miR223 in mitochondria and in vitro.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that YBAP1 binds miR223 in mitochondria and in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on immunoprecipitation and EMSA data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Knockout of YBAP1 does not change exosome secretion.
source: Although knockout of YBAP1 did not change exosome secretion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a), RT-qPCR analysis showed that miR223 decreased twofold in mitochondria but increased eightfold in exosomes purified from mutant and WT cells, respectively (Figure 5c).
evidence: Supported by CD63-Nluc luminescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claim: miR223 decreases twofold in mitochondria but increases eightfold in exosomes in YBAP1 KO cells compared to WT cells.
source: Although knockout of YBAP1 did not change exosome secretion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a), RT-qPCR analysis showed that miR223 decreased twofold in mitochondria but increased eightfold in exosomes purified from mutant and WT cells, respectively (Figure 5c).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The inverse relationship between mitochondrial and exosomal miR223 in YBAP1 KO cells is consistent with a role for YBAP1 protein in the retention of miR223 in mitochondria.
source: This apparent inverse relationship is consistent with a role for YBAP1 protein in the retention of miR223 in mitochondria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that YBAP1 KO decreases mitochondrial and increases exosomal miR223.

claim: YBX1 puncta colocalize with mitochondria.
source: To explore this possibility, we visualized endogenous YBX1 and YBAP1 by IF and observed YBX1 puncta colocalized with mitochondria (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6a-b.

claim: Time-lapse imaging shows YBX1 puncta in close proximity to mitochondria or endosomes, followed by transfer between them.
source: Time-lapse imaging showed YBX1 puncta in close proximity to mitochondria or endosomes, followed quickly by transfer between them (Figure 6c and d).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 6c-d.

claim: miR223 stored in mitochondria may be captured in a tighter interaction with YBX1 in P-bodies and delivered to endosomes for sorting and secretion in exosomes.
source: Taken together, these data suggest a mechanism whereby miR223 stored in mitochondria, possibly sequestered by YBAP1, may be captured in a tighter interaction with YBX1 in P-bodies and delivered to endosomes for sorting and secretion in exosomes.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the collective data from the study.

claim: The miR223 sequence motif UCAGU may represent a binding site or structural feature required for sorting.
source: We found that miR223 specifically binds a 'cold shock' domain (CSD) of YBX1 through a 5' proximal sequence motif UCAGU that may represent a binding site or structural feature required for sorting.
evidence: This is speculation about whether the motif is a binding site or structural feature.

claim: P-bodies have been seen in association with mitochondria.
source: In other earlier work, P-bodies were seen in association with mitochondria (Huang et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Huang et al., 2011.

claim: The cell-free reaction provides a model that mimics aspects of exosome biogenesis.
source: We concluded that our cell-free reaction provides a model that mimics aspects of exosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that GW4869 inhibits both the cell-free reaction and exosome secretion.

claim: GW4869 inhibits the protection of CD63-luciferase and miR-223 in the cell-free assay at concentrations known to inhibit the activity of NS2.
source: In our cell-free assay, GW4869 inhibited the protection of CD63-luciferase and miR-223 at concentrations known to inhibit the activity of NS2 in partially purified enzyme fractions (Shurtleff et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shurtleff et al., 2016.

claim: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of YBX1 includes an intrinsically disordered domain (IDR) that promotes the formation of a liquid-liquid phase separation likely responsible for the organization of YBX1 in P-bodies.
source: The C-terminal domain (CTD) includes an intrinsically disordered domain (IDR) that promotes the formation of a liquid-liquid phase separation likely responsible for the organization of YBX1 in P-bodies (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2021.

claim: Two separate sorting signals, a 5'UGGA and a 3'UUU, on miR122 are bound by the RNA-binding protein La en route to secretion in exosomes by the breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231.
source: In other work using a similar approach, we identified two separate sorting signals, a 5'UGGA and a 3'UUU, on miR122 to which the RNA-binding protein La binds en route to secretion in exosomes by the breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 (Temoche-Diaz et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Temoche-Diaz et al., 2019.

claim: miRNAs with a GGAG sorting motif recognized by a sumolyated form of hnRNPA2B1 are enriched in exosomes.
source: miRNAs with a GGAG sorting motif recognized by a sumolyated form of hnRNPA2B1 was shown to be enriched in exosomes (Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013.

claim: The sequence AAUGC is enriched in exosomal miRNA and dependent on the RNA-binding protein FMR1 for miRNA secretion.
source: Another sequence, AAUGC, was found to be enriched in exosomal miRNA and dependent on the RNA-binding protein FMR1 for miRNA secretion (Wozniak et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wozniak et al., 2020.

claim: Diverse cell lines and likely tissues invoke distinct sorting signals decoded by different RNA-binding proteins.
source: Diverse cell lines and likely tissues appear to invoke distinct sorting signals decoded by different RNA-binding proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of multiple different sorting signals and RNA-binding proteins in different cell types.

claim: Many of the RNA-binding proteins may engage in biomolecular condensates such as P-bodies as a mechanism to sort RNAs for secretion.
source: Many of the proteins may engage in biomolecular condensates such as P-bodies as a mechanism to sort RNAs for secretion (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2021.

claim: miR223 appears to be an example of a number of small nuclear-encoded RNAs localized to mitochondria.
source: miR223 appears to be an example of a number of small nuclear-encoded RNAs localized to mitochondria (Jeandard et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jeandard et al., 2019.

claim: For miRNAs with no obvious mitochondrial genome target, the function remains unclear.
source: In some cases these RNAs, such as tRNAs, serve an essential function such as in mitochondrial protein synthesis, however, for miRNAs with no obvious mitochondrial genome target, the function remains unclear (Jeandard et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jeandard et al., 2019.

claim: The highly selective nature of miRNA sorting and secretion in exosomes suggests an important role in the trafficking of miRNAs between cells.
source: The highly selective nature of miRNA sorting and secretion in exosomes suggests an important role in the trafficking of miRNAs between cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed selectivity of miRNA sorting.

claim: Numerous studies have suggested a role for secreted miRNAs in recipient cells.
source: Numerous studies have suggested a role for secreted miRNAs in recipient cells (Cha et al., 2015; Mittelbrunn et al., 2011; Pegtel et al., 2010; Valadi et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The extremely low abundance and copy number of miRNAs per vesicle is hard to reconcile with a functional role of secreted miRNA in recipient cells.
source: Nonetheless, as miRNAs ordinarily act stoichiometrically on target mRNAs, the extremely low abundance and copy number of miRNAs/vesicle is hard to reconcile with such a functional role of secreted miRNA (Chevillet et al., 2014; Shurtleff et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chevillet et al., 2014 and Shurtleff et al., 2017.

claim: The bulk of cellular miR223 is held within mitochondria.
source: Our observation that the bulk of cellular miR223 is held within mitochondria suggests an alternative role in some structural or regulatory process, perhaps essential for mitochondrial homeostasis, controlled by the selective extraction of unwanted miRNA into RNA granules and further by secretion in exosomes (Figure 7).
evidence: Supported by subcellular fractionation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The localization of miR223 in mitochondria suggests an alternative role in some structural or regulatory process, perhaps essential for mitochondrial homeostasis.
source: Our observation that the bulk of cellular miR223 is held within mitochondria suggests an alternative role in some structural or regulatory process, perhaps essential for mitochondrial homeostasis, controlled by the selective extraction of unwanted miRNA into RNA granules and further by secretion in exosomes (Figure 7).
evidence: This is speculation about the potential function of mitochondrial miR223.

claim: Mitochondrial homeostasis may be controlled by the selective extraction of unwanted miRNA into RNA granules and further by secretion in exosomes.
source: Our observation that the bulk of cellular miR223 is held within mitochondria suggests an alternative role in some structural or regulatory process, perhaps essential for mitochondrial homeostasis, controlled by the selective extraction of unwanted miRNA into RNA granules and further by secretion in exosomes (Figure 7).
evidence: This is speculation about a potential mechanism for mitochondrial homeostasis.

claim: Cytosolic miR223 is enriched in mitochondria where it may be sequestered by a weak interaction with YBAP1.
source: Cytosolic miR223 is enriched in mitochondria where it may be sequestered by a weak interaction with YBAP1.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 7, based on the collective data.

claim: Cytoplasmic YBX1 interacts more tightly with miR223 which may drive the removal of miR223 from mitochondria.
source: Cytoplasmic YBX1 interacts more tightly with miR223 which may drive the removal of miR223 from mitochondria.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 7, based on the collective data.

claim: YBX1 in RNA granules may accumulate miR223 removed from mitochondria.
source: YBX1 in RNA granules may accumulate miR223 removed from mitochondria.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 7, based on the collective data.

claim: YBX1 puncta may give rise to small particles carrying miR223 for uptake into endosomes and secretion in exosomes.
source: YBX1 puncta may give rise to small particles carrying miR223 for uptake into endosomes and secretion in exosomes.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 7, based on the collective data.
